record.original_question: Liouville-type assertion on CR 3-manifolds. On a CR 3-manifold one can always define a Carnot-Caratheodory metric. A homeomorphism between two strongly pseudoconvex CR 3-manifolds is called conformal if it maps infinitesimal spheres with respect to a Carnot-Caratheodory metric to infinitesimal spheres. Is a conformal homeomorphism CR?

evidence.quote: Problem 12.3.1 (New) (Liouville type assertion on CR 3-manifolds) On a CR 3-manifold one can always define a Carnot-Caratheodory metric. A homeomorphism between two strongly pseudoconvex CR 3-manifolds is called conformal if it maps infinitesimal spheres with respect to a Carnot-Caratheodory metric to infinitesimal spheres. Is a conformal homeomorphism CR? -Puqi Tang, tang@math.purdue.edu

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^3,H,J)$ and $(N^3,H',J')$ be strongly pseudoconvex CR 3-manifolds. Recall that a CR 3-manifold carries a contact distribution $H\subset TM$ of rank 2 endowed with an almost complex structure $J:H\to H$, and that after fixing a pseudo-Hermitian contact form $\theta$ (with $d\theta(\cdot,J\cdot)$ positive definite on $H$) one obtains an associated Carnot–Carathéodory metric $d_{CC}$: the distance between two points is the infimum of the lengths (measured by the Levi form) of horizontal curves joining them. For $p\in M$ and $r>0$ let $B_{CC}(p,r)=\{q:d_{CC}(p,q)<r\}$. 

Given a homeomorphism $f:M\to N$ and a point $p\in M$, define
$$L_f(p,r)=\sup_{d_{CC}(p,q)=r} d'_{CC}(f(p),f(q)), \qquad \ell_f(p,r)=\inf_{d_{CC}(p,q)=r} d'_{CC}(f(p),f(q)).$$
Call $f$ conformal at $p$ if $\lim_{r\to 0^+} L_f(p,r)/\ell_f(p,r)=1$, i.e. $f$ sends infinitesimal CC-spheres centered at $p$ to sets that are asymptotically CC-spheres centered at $f(p)$. Call $f$ conformal on $M$ if it is conformal at every point.

A homeomorphism $f:M\to N$ is said to be CR if it is a diffeomorphism with $df(H)=H'$ and $df\circ J=J'\circ df$ on $H$ (or the corresponding statement for anti-CR).

Question: Must every conformal homeomorphism $f:M\to N$ between strongly pseudoconvex CR 3-manifolds be a CR (or anti-CR) mapping?
artifact.status_search_result: Related results are known: Korányi–Reimann showed that smooth 1-quasiconformal mappings between domains of the Heisenberg group are CR or anti-CR (restrictions of SU(n+1,1) actions), and later work extended this to tight/Goursat Carnot groups and to 1-quasiconformal homeomorphisms on CR manifolds with symmetries. However, the specific Liouville-type assertion as stated — that any homeomorphism between strongly pseudoconvex CR 3-manifolds preserving infinitesimal CC-spheres must be CR — does not appear to have a definitively cited resolution in the searched literature, so the status is treated as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Conformal and CR mappings on Carnot groups
status_evidence.snippet: On a tight stratified group a homeomorphism is 1-quasiconformal if and only if it is CR or anti-CR.
status_evidence.claim: Related Liouville-type results connecting 1-quasiconformality and CR maps are established for Carnot groups.

status_evidence.title: 1-Quasiconformal Mappings and CR Mappings on Goursat Groups
status_evidence.snippet: 1-quasiconformal mappings on Goursat groups are CR or anti-CR under appropriate conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions of the Heisenberg-group Liouville-type theorem to other nilpotent groups exist but do not directly settle the stated CR 3-manifold question.
